world.summary: dockInReach (step.ts) now moors a ship whose hull overlaps the berth tile or any of its eight neighbours, where a diagonal neighbour counts only if one of the two tiles it shares with the berth is navigable. Otherwise it falls back to reach plus a clear run. dockRadius stays 384. Per the operator addendum from design challenge attempt 5, 'beside' is decided from every tile the hull square overlaps, in both dockInReach and the test oracle. Removed the land spur at (20-21, 28) from the sketch; the map is mirrored, so this removes all four copies. Regenerated slice-sea.tmj and sliceSea.ts with `npm run map:build -- --from-sketch`, and every validator passes. The sketch writer moved into scripts/build-map.ts behind --from-sketch; sketch.ts is deleted and sliceSeaSketch.ts has no Node import. maps.test.ts now reads the sketch through ?raw and fails on any node: specifier. Fixed the stale sketch.ts references in the test title, the header comments, README.md, assets/source/maps/README.md and docs/architecture.md. The docking paragraph in architecture.md now uses the addendum's sentence and is 722 characters, one shorter than before. Tests in simulation.test.ts: the diagonal half of the old corner test now moors, and its shoal-segment hullPathIsClear assertions are kept. New tests: the pinch guard with land and with shoal; behind land with dockRadius 640; the head-on approach (heading 48, offsets -336 and -368) on the synthetic island and on the real dock (23, 27); and the addendum's column-25 case at (23, 27) for x from 6400 to 6479. The old sweep is replaced by a start-grid sweep: 64-sub-unit sea starts at Chebyshev distance 2-4 from the berth, every 8th heading into an open side, speeds 0, half and full. It covers the synthetic island and all 8 real docks, 97,326 lanes. Every step is checked against an oracle in the test that uses terrain lookups only. Resting places are an exact list of 18 entries, 2 per dock, and the outcome counts must add up to the number of lanes. With the spur temporarily restored, the sweep failed on Palm Key, south dock at (22, 29) and (21, 29). After removing it, both are gone. The sweep takes about 7.5-10 s. The old lateral-offset corner test and the sweep got a 30 s timeout, because the old test took 9-12 s under machine load (load average 8), with the new step.ts and with the old one. Checks run: npm ci; npm run typecheck (pass); npm run test:unit (560 passed); npm run test:integration (38 passed); npm run build (pass); the full Playwright suite with the JSON reporter (6/6 passed, check-report OK); sail-and-dock with --repeat-each=5 (5/5 passed). Decisions: the operator addendum from design challenge attempt 5 (hull-overlap tiles, the column-25 test at (23, 27), the Chebyshev ring, stale sketch.ts references, the docs sentence) was adopted as binding.
open_assumptions: A lane ends once the ship is more than 6 tiles (Chebyshev) from the berth, because with a fixed heading each axis moves one way only. A lane still under way after 400 steps counts as a failure.
Removing the spur changes no validator result; I checked this with map:build.
packages/content/src/raw.d.ts (not owned) has a comment saying only the drift test uses ?raw. That is now slightly stale, and I left it unchanged.
I added a 30 s timeout to the existing lateral-offset corner test. I did not change its assertions.

findings.message: Stale descriptions of the old reach-only rule remain in owned files. simulation.test.ts:506-508 (title 'as soon as it is within reach' and its comment), simulation.test.ts:660-663 ('moors on the first step it starts within the dock's reach with a clear run'), and tests/e2e/sea.spec.ts:102-104 and 120-121 still describe mooring as 'within the dock's reach with a clear run'. The test in maps.test.ts only matches /["'`]node:/, so a bare builtin specifier such as `from "fs"` would pass. The task's literal requirement ('any `node:` import') is met; the comment overclaims. Either tighten the comment or also reject bare builtin names.
findings.requirement: A unit test reads `sliceSeaSketch.ts`'s source (the existing `?raw` pattern) and fails on any `node:` import.

findings.message: scripts/build-map.ts:33-38 runs the --from-sketch write before anything else and ignores --check. So `npm run map:check -- --from-sketch` (or `tsx scripts/build-map.ts --check --from-sketch`) overwrites assets/source/maps/slice-sea.tmj, although the header says '--check writes nothing'. The .tmj is also written before the subset check and the validators run, so a failing sketch leaves a rewritten .tmj behind. Refuse the flag combination, or skip the write under --check.
findings.requirement: Move the file writing into the typechecked `scripts/build-map.ts` (for example `npm run map:build -- --from-sketch`)

findings.message: Informational, accepted by the task's own allowance. Each real south dock keeps a resting place in the berth's own row, two tiles out: for Palm Key's south dock (23,27), (25,27) with x >= 6480. There a ship driven due north grounds about 466 sub-units from the berth centre, with open water (24,27) between it and the berth. Holding E does nothing and the HUD offers no hint. It is on the exact list with a reason and fits the decision that non-adjacent positions don't moor. A player may still feel it as a near miss one tile from the berth-side tile.
findings.requirement: unless its (dock, rest tile) pair is in an exact hard-coded list

findings.message: The sweep's oracle (simulation.test.ts:686-731) decides 'beside' from every tile the 80-sub-unit hull overlaps, not from the tile under the ship's centre as the pinned text says. The test at simulation.test.ts:590-605 (column 25 at dock (23, 27)) asserts mooring in exactly the case where the two readings differ: centre tile (25, 27) is two tiles from the berth and more than 384 from its centre. The worker cites an 'operator addendum from design challenge attempt 5'. That matches challenge-5.json's simpler_alternative, but it appears in neither the pinned task text nor decisions.md (both sha256 values are unchanged from attempt 5 to attempt 6). So the sweep fully checks the implemented rule both ways (moors when accepted, never when refused), but it does not check the pinned centre-tile rule. The operator should confirm the addendum is binding.
findings.requirement: The oracle accepts the step's start position when its tile is the berth tile or an orthogonal neighbour, or a diagonal neighbour with at least one shared tile navigable, or when the berth centre is within the reach with a clear run.

findings.message: No test has two docks that both qualify at once, so the choice of the nearest berth in dockInReach (step.ts:102-116, including the new `distance >= bestDistance` early continue and the switch from reach+1 to POSITIVE_INFINITY) is never exercised. Every synthetic sea has one dock, and on the slice sea no sweep lane reaches a second dock's neighbourhood (challenge-6.json says the same), so the sweep's all-docks oracle never compares competing docks.
findings.requirement: returns the nearest berth whose tile is the ship's tile or one of its eight neighbours

findings.message: The sweep reports the lane, mooring, rest-near and sailed-past counts only through `annotate` (simulation.test.ts:833). The unit check's reporter doesn't print it: the candidate's unit log (log-2-d597b231d029) shows only the test name and 9736ms. The counts, including the claimed 97,326 lanes, appear in no verification artifact. The sum check `moorings + restsNear + sailedPast !== lanes` and the exact rest list, which must match both ways, do guard against silent skips, so this is evidence visibility only.
findings.requirement: Lanes that sail past without grounding near the berth need no entry: the test counts and reports them.

From the overnight session of 2026-09-24/25. The operator is asleep and asked the assistant to decide, record each decision, and use the workflow for the code.

- sea-compact-fixes-001's general reviewer approved the candidate `df8fad0`. The coverage reviewer blocked it with a P1: the approach sweep skipped lanes. - The fix is a generous rule, not a longer reach: a ship on the berth tile or any of its eight neighbours moors when E is pressed, even across a corner. Right beside the dock means docked. The reach stays 384, and a berth behind land (not adjacent) still doesn't moor.
